- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.2) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent low trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; dampen early forecast peaks.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.2 → +0.6), model misreads momentum; apply smoothing filter to avoid abrupt directional shifts.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% over 3–5 days, model underestimates trend; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to capture momentum.
